content: 1. Sulfasalazine increases the anticoagulant effect, while mistletoe decreases it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring and caution are advised. 2. Moexipril and sulfasalazine may mutually increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms not fully understood. Sulfasalazine reduces the effectiveness of moexipril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 3. NSAIDs reduce the synthesis of vasodilating renal prostaglandins, potentially impairing fluid homeostasis and diminishing the antihypertensive effects of certain medications. Close monitoring is necessary. 4. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of sulfasalazine due to competition for plasma protein binding. Additionally, as a BCRP inhibitor, momelotinib may increase the exposure and adverse effects of BCRP substrates. Dose adjustments for BCRP substrates may be required, and close monitoring is essential. 5. Sulfasalazine decreases the effects of moxisylyte through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Sulfasalazine increases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by competing for renal tubular clearance. Close monitoring and caution are necessary. 7. Nabumetone and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Nabumetone also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 8. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of nadolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use with nadolol and sulfasalazine may increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Sulfasalazine decreases the effects of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Close monitoring is required. 10. Naproxen and sulfasalazine both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Naproxen also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is necessary. 11. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of nebivolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use with nebivolol and sulfasalazine may increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Nefazodone and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Close monitoring and caution are necessary. 13. Sulfasalazine increases neomycin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants. The clinical significance is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 14. Sulfasalazine increases anticoagulation, while nettle decreases it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Sulfasalazine and noni juice both increase serum potassium levels. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 16. Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium levels, while norepinephrine decreases it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Sulfasalazine and ofloxacin may interact, increasing the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement in the brain. Close monitoring is necessary. 18. Olmesartan and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of olmesartan via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Otesecazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity of BCRP substrates, including sulfasalazine. Starting with the lowest dose of BCRP substrates or reducing their dose is advised. Close monitoring is essential. 20. Oxaprozin and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Oxaprozin also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is necessary. 21. Sulfasalazine and panax ginseng both increase anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 22. Parecoxib and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Parecoxib also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is necessary. 23. Sulfasalazine increases paromomycin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is primarily observed in preterm infants. The clinical significance is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 24. Paroxetine and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Close monitoring and caution are necessary. 25. Sulfasalazine and pau d'arco both increase anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 26. Pegaspargase enhances the effects of sulfasalazine through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of bleeding events. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 27. Sulfasalazine increases pemetrexed levels through an unspecified mechanism. Co-administration with NSAIDs with long elimination half-lives should be avoided or interrupted for at least five days before, the day of, and two days after pemetrexed administration. If co-administration is necessary, patients should be closely monitored for toxicity, including myelosuppression, renal toxicity, and gastrointestinal toxicity. 28. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of penbutolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use with penbutolol and sulfasalazine may increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Perindopril and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of perindopril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Pexidartinib and sulfasalazine both increase toxicity. Pexidartinib is associated with hepatotoxicity, and co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. Close monitoring is necessary. 31. Phenindione and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of phenoxybenzamine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis. Close monitoring is required. 33. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of phentolamine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis. Close monitoring is required. 34. Sulfasalazine and phytoestrogens both increase anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 35. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of pindolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use with pindolol and sulfasalazine may increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 36. Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium levels, while pirbuterol decreases it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 37. Piroxicam and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Piroxicam also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is necessary. 38. Ponatinib increases sulfasalazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 39. Sulfasalazine and potassium acid phosphate both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Sulfasalazine and potassium citrate both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of prazosin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis. Close monitoring is required. 43. Prednisolone and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Prednisolone decreases sulfasalazine levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 44. Prednisone and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Prednisone decreases sulfasalazine levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 45. Pretomanid increases sulfasalazine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, and co-administration with hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. Close monitoring is necessary. 46. Sulfasalazine increases probenecid levels by competing for renal tubular clearance but decreases its effects through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 47. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of propranolol via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Long-term NSAID use with propranolol and sulfasalazine may increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 48. Protamine and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Quinapril and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of quinapril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Ramipril and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of ramipril via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Regorafenib increases sulfasalazine levels by inhibiting BCRP transport. Co-administration with BCRP substrates may increase systemic exposure and related toxicity. Close monitoring is necessary. 52. Sulfasalazine and reishi both enhance anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Ropeginterferon alfa-2b and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity, leading to additive myelosuppression. Co-administration should be avoided, and patients should be monitored for excessive myelosuppression. 54. Rose hips increase sulfasalazine levels by decreasing renal clearance, while sulfasalazine decreases rose hips levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 55. Sacubitril/valsartan and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of sacubitril/valsartan via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Safinamide increases sulfasalazine levels by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. BCRP substrates should be monitored for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. Close monitoring is necessary. 57. Salicylates (non-ASA) and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Salicylates also increase sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 58. Sulfasalazine increases serum potassium levels, while salmeterol decreases it. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 59. Salsalate and sulfasalazine both enhance anticoagulation and increase serum potassium levels. Salsalate also increases sulfasalazine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 60. Sertraline and sulfasalazine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. SSRIs inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets. Close monitoring and caution are necessary. 61. Sulfasalazine and Siberian ginseng both enhance anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 62. Sulfasalazine reduces the effects of silodosin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. NSAIDs decrease prostaglandin synthesis. Close monitoring is required. 63. Sodium bicarbonate may alter sulfasalazine levels due to increased renal tubular reabsorption caused by elevated pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 64. Sodium citrate/citric acid may alter sulfasalazine levels due to increased renal tubular reabsorption caused by elevated pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so close monitoring is recommended. 65. Sulfasalazine and sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid may increase each other's toxicity, potentially causing fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 66. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases sulfasalazine levels by inhibiting the drug transporter BCRP. Close monitoring is necessary.
